# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (role function) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit-corporation structure makes safety a product and commercialization constraint, not simply a research message. Enterprise adoption must be repeatable without weakening expectations around reliable, interpretable,
and steerable systems.

The operating tension is converting advanced-model demand into durable, governed business outcomes through third parties while retaining consistent technical, security, and adoption standards. This is less a conventional channel-coverage
problem than a quality-control problem at ecosystem scale.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier AI safety and research company, founded in 2021, whose flagship product family is Claude. It is an American public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco.

Its archetype is a product-led, developer- and enterprise-platform hybrid. It wins by making Claude useful for complex knowledge work, data analysis, and software development while positioning safety, accuracy, and security as core adoption
attributes.

The central commercial challenge is to turn a rapidly evolving AI product surface into repeatable enterprise deployments. That requires a clear boundary between product capabilities, customer operating change, and partner-delivered
implementation.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic operates where model quality, safety posture, enterprise trust, and distribution reinforce one another. Its company mission emphasizes reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems, creating a higher bar for how external
implementation teams represent the product.

Claude serves both direct users and organizations, increasing the importance of consistent experience across self-serve, enterprise, and API-based adoption paths. The practical pressure is to prevent fragmented partner implementations from
becoming the customer’s experience of Anthropic.

The decision-rights tension is likely between speed of ecosystem-led expansion and central control over technical patterns, product feedback, deployment quality, and safety-aligned use.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Dario Amodei is co-founder and chief executive officer. Daniela Amodei is co-founder and president. Their founding context connects the company’s commercial expansion to an explicit AI-safety mission.

Relevant stakeholders are likely to span Partnerships, enterprise go-to-market, product, engineering, developer-facing teams, security and trust functions, and customer adoption teams. The most consequential alignment is between field
demand for deployable solutions and product teams’ need for structured, validated deployment feedback.

An effective internal posture at Anthropic should respect that technical credibility is not separate from business credibility: the company’s claims about reliability and steerability make implementation quality a leadership concern.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude is positioned for complex problem solving, including analysis, coding, and work involving difficult information tasks. That creates architecture conversations beyond model selection: workflow design, API integration, evaluation,
access controls, user enablement, and operational ownership.

Anthropic publishes a Claude Enterprise deployment framework organized around technical setup, change management and launch, enablement and training, and scaling adoption. This signals that enterprise success is treated as an operating
lifecycle rather than a one-time technical installation.

Claude Code configuration is included in enterprise administration guidance. That makes developer and engineering adoption an important part of the enterprise platform story, alongside business-user rollout.

The company’s safety orientation raises the value of reusable architectural standards. Partners need more than demos; they need deployment patterns that support accurate use, appropriate governance, and measurable adoption.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Partnerships are material because enterprise AI adoption often depends on a customer’s existing cloud, consulting, and technology ecosystem. Anthropic’s implementation guidance and enterprise education materials indicate a need to make
deployment knowledge transferable beyond a central internal team.

The ecosystem motion should be judged by whether partners can carry a coherent technical narrative from qualification through implementation and scaled adoption. A partner-led engagement is successful only if it protects Claude’s product
experience while expanding reach.

High-value partner assets in this environment are likely to be repeatable solution patterns, deployment playbooks, enablement material, adoption frameworks, and a disciplined route for partner feedback into product and engineering.

The technical close matters disproportionately: customers and partners will need confidence not only that a model works, but that it can be introduced into existing workflows with accountable controls and durable user adoption.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s current product positioning emphasizes Claude as an assistant for complex work, while its enterprise materials formalize the path from setup through organization-wide adoption. That combination raises the urgency of converting
isolated usage into scalable operating programs.

The inclusion of Claude Code in enterprise administration guidance broadens the adoption surface from general knowledge work into technical teams. Partners need to support distinct user groups without creating separate, incompatible
deployment models.

Frontier AI competition increases the premium on execution after the initial model evaluation. As enterprise buyers compare alternatives, implementation velocity, governance confidence, and realized workflow value become differentiation
points alongside model capability.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building repeatable enterprise AI deployment patterns rather than isolated proofs of concept.
- Translating advanced AI capabilities into governed workflows and measurable adoption.
- Establishing reusable reference architectures, evaluation practices, and implementation playbooks.
- Balancing ecosystem scale with consistency in security, safety, and customer experience.
- Supporting both business-user and developer adoption paths for AI platforms.
- Operating credibly with technical executives, implementation leaders, and commercial stakeholders.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s enterprise deployment model recognizes that launch is only the first phase; durable adoption requires technical, organizational, and enablement coordination.
- Claude’s use across analysis, complex knowledge work, and coding increases the need for implementation patterns that work across user populations.
- The public-benefit and safety orientation makes partner-delivered quality especially important as the ecosystem expands.
- The compelling challenge is scaling technical partner capability without allowing each deployment to become a bespoke interpretation of the platform.
- A useful conversation starter is the handoff from technical setup to change management, training, and scaled usage.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, outcomes, scope, leadership experience, technical depth, and partnership results must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (role function) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit-corporation structure makes safety a product and commercialization constraint, not simply a research message. Enterprise adoption must be repeatable without weakening expectations around reliable, interpretable,
and steerable systems.

The operating tension is converting advanced-model demand into durable, governed business outcomes through third parties while retaining consistent technical, security, and adoption standards. This is less a conventional channel-coverage
problem than a quality-control problem at ecosystem scale.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier AI safety and research company, founded in 2021, whose flagship product family is Claude. It is an American public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco.

Its archetype is a product-led, developer- and enterprise-platform hybrid. It wins by making Claude useful for complex knowledge work, data analysis, and software development while positioning safety, accuracy, and security as core adoption
attributes.

The central commercial challenge is to turn a rapidly evolving AI product surface into repeatable enterprise deployments. That requires a clear boundary between product capabilities, customer operating change, and partner-delivered
implementation.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic operates where model quality, safety posture, enterprise trust, and distribution reinforce one another. Its company mission emphasizes reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems, creating a higher bar for how external
implementation teams represent the product.

Claude serves both direct users and organizations, increasing the importance of consistent experience across self-serve, enterprise, and API-based adoption paths. The practical pressure is to prevent fragmented partner implementations from
becoming the customer’s experience of Anthropic.

The decision-rights tension is likely between speed of ecosystem-led expansion and central control over technical patterns, product feedback, deployment quality, and safety-aligned use.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Dario Amodei is co-founder and chief executive officer. Daniela Amodei is co-founder and president. Their founding context connects the company’s commercial expansion to an explicit AI-safety mission.

Relevant stakeholders are likely to span Partnerships, enterprise go-to-market, product, engineering, developer-facing teams, security and trust functions, and customer adoption teams. The most consequential alignment is between field
demand for deployable solutions and product teams’ need for structured, validated deployment feedback.

An effective internal posture at Anthropic should respect that technical credibility is not separate from business credibility: the company’s claims about reliability and steerability make implementation quality a leadership concern.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude is positioned for complex problem solving, including analysis, coding, and work involving difficult information tasks. That creates architecture conversations beyond model selection: workflow design, API integration, evaluation,
access controls, user enablement, and operational ownership.

Anthropic publishes a Claude Enterprise deployment framework organized around technical setup, change management and launch, enablement and training, and scaling adoption. This signals that enterprise success is treated as an operating
lifecycle rather than a one-time technical installation.

Claude Code configuration is included in enterprise administration guidance. That makes developer and engineering adoption an important part of the enterprise platform story, alongside business-user rollout.

The company’s safety orientation raises the value of reusable architectural standards. Partners need more than demos; they need deployment patterns that support accurate use, appropriate governance, and measurable adoption.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Partnerships are material because enterprise AI adoption often depends on a customer’s existing cloud, consulting, and technology ecosystem. Anthropic’s implementation guidance and enterprise education materials indicate a need to make
deployment knowledge transferable beyond a central internal team.

The ecosystem motion should be judged by whether partners can carry a coherent technical narrative from qualification through implementation and scaled adoption. A partner-led engagement is successful only if it protects Claude’s product
experience while expanding reach.

High-value partner assets in this environment are likely to be repeatable solution patterns, deployment playbooks, enablement material, adoption frameworks, and a disciplined route for partner feedback into product and engineering.

The technical close matters disproportionately: customers and partners will need confidence not only that a model works, but that it can be introduced into existing workflows with accountable controls and durable user adoption.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s current product positioning emphasizes Claude as an assistant for complex work, while its enterprise materials formalize the path from setup through organization-wide adoption. That combination raises the urgency of converting
isolated usage into scalable operating programs.

The inclusion of Claude Code in enterprise administration guidance broadens the adoption surface from general knowledge work into technical teams. Partners need to support distinct user groups without creating separate, incompatible
deployment models.

Frontier AI competition increases the premium on execution after the initial model evaluation. As enterprise buyers compare alternatives, implementation velocity, governance confidence, and realized workflow value become differentiation
points alongside model capability.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building repeatable enterprise AI deployment patterns rather than isolated proofs of concept.
- Translating advanced AI capabilities into governed workflows and measurable adoption.
- Establishing reusable reference architectures, evaluation practices, and implementation playbooks.
- Balancing ecosystem scale with consistency in security, safety, and customer experience.
- Supporting both business-user and developer adoption paths for AI platforms.
- Operating credibly with technical executives, implementation leaders, and commercial stakeholders.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s enterprise deployment model recognizes that launch is only the first phase; durable adoption requires technical, organizational, and enablement coordination.
- Claude’s use across analysis, complex knowledge work, and coding increases the need for implementation patterns that work across user populations.
- The public-benefit and safety orientation makes partner-delivered quality especially important as the ecosystem expands.
- The compelling challenge is scaling technical partner capability without allowing each deployment to become a bespoke interpretation of the platform.
- A useful conversation starter is the handoff from technical setup to change management, training, and scaled usage.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, outcomes, scope, leadership experience, technical depth, and partnership results must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.
